text:
sasha: Heads-up — saw a cluster of Pending pods in eng-models-eu last night. Symptoms: pods stuck for >10m requesting `nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb`, only a handful of nodes expose that slice size. CA didn't kick in to add matching nodes.
ryan: Ugh, fragmentation again. Did we enable mixed MIG profiles last deploy? :thinking:
lia: We did flip the MIG toggle for the eu pool to `mixed` on Tue (to test smaller workloads). That gives us 1g + 2g on the same nodes, but scheduling is getting weird.
sasha: Exactly. The CA sees there are nodes with free GPU capacity but not the specific MIG slice the pod asks for, so it marks pods as unschedulable instead of scaling.
ryan: Two quick ideas: (1) dedicate a nodepool with only 1g slices and nodeSelector for latency-sensitive jobs, (2) switch short batch jobs to time-slice-enabled T4s where possible.
lia: Note on time-slicing: it helps for sub-second token jobs but increases GPU utilization variance. For model servers that need KV cache it's bad. Also time-slicing isn't available on the dedicated reserved pools due to firmware constraints.
sasha: Agree. Cost tradeoff: many 1g slices => more nodes => higher baseline infra cost. But better pod placement and less over-provisioning.
ryan: Also the cluster-autoscaler flags matter. Today we're using `--expander=least-waste` which can avoid scaling if it thinks existing nodes could fit the pod with bin-packing, but it doesn't reason about MIG slices. We might need to set `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` or run a custom expander for GPU shape.
lia: I sketched a short pod example showing the nodeSelector + toleration pattern we should use for the 1g-specific pool:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: small-gpu-job
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    gpu.mig.redwood.com/profile: "1g"
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-profile"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "1g"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  containers:
  - name: runner
    image: redwood/model-runner:canary
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb: 1
```

ryan: Nice. Ops suggestion: create `gpu-eu-1g` pool with a small min-size (2) and aggressive scale-up policy. Then update our queueing/helm chart to use nodeSelector for model-inference-srv (canary first).
ops-bot: Autoscaler notice: scaled up +3 nodes to gpu-eu-1g at 2026-12-03T18:20:03Z due to 12 pending pods.
sasha: Can someone run a quick smoke deploy to canary and watch the scale path? If that looks good we'll promote to prod.
lia: I'll do it. Quick checklist I also want to confirm:
- ensure kubelet reports MIG tooling labels (`gpu.mig.redwood.com/profile`) on node registration
- update scale-down `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 10m for GPU pools so we don't thrash
- add CA webhook to treat MIG unschedulable reason as "needs different node group" fallback

ryan: For the CA webhook idea, we can add a filter that looks at `FailedScheduling` reasons containing `no matching MIG` and annotate the pod so the expander picks the right nodeGroup.
sasha: Good call. Also watch cross-region fallback: if eu-west1 is low on quota, we should allow fallback to eu-west4 for non-PII jobs. That requires a policy change in smart-routing.
lia: I'll open a tiny RFC for `gpu-eu-fallback` routing flag and a quota/chargeback note. TL;DR: prefer local, but allow cross-region for non-sensitive batch inference when eu is constrained.
ryan: After canary, if all green, plan: create `gpu-eu-1g` nodepool, add taint `gpu-profile=1g:NoSchedule`, update charts, and a small CA expander tweak. Ops runbook updated.
sasha: Thanks team. If anyone notices weird pod evictions after scale-down ping me. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline started for `inference/canary` — job #4582. Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/4582
lia: Monitoring spike looks good so far — pods scheduled onto new nodes. Will report back in 30m.
ryan: If we see persistent fragmentation at 70% utilization we should revisit using fewer, larger profiles + smarter application-level multiplexing.
sasha: Agreed. Closing this thread after canary results. Cheers.
